title: Designing and Planning a Solution (Section 1, ~25%)

lessons.title: Business Requirements and the Well-Architected Framework
lessons.summary: Functional and non-functional requirements, KPIs, build-buy-modify-deprecate and the framework pillars.
takeaways: Convert business goals into measurable functional and non-functional requirements, with explicit constraints.
Disposition each workload: build, buy, modify or deprecate; justify with KPIs, ROI and TCO.
The framework pillars: operational excellence, security, reliability, cost optimization, performance optimization, sustainability.
Always state the trade-off; prefer managed, cloud-first designs unless a requirement says otherwise.

lessons.title: High Availability, Disaster Recovery and Scalability
lessons.summary: RTO and RPO, regional and multi-regional design, failover, backup and recovery.
takeaways: Derive RTO, RPO and availability targets from business impact; each extra nine costs more.
Zone failure: regional managed services. Region failure: second region plus a global load balancer and a replicated database.
DR patterns trade cost for recovery speed: backup/restore, pilot light, warm standby, hot.
Match the database replication model to RPO; test restores and failovers regularly.

lessons.title: Choosing Compute: Compute Engine, GKE, Cloud Run and Functions
lessons.summary: Map workloads to platform products, machine types, Spot VMs and specialised hardware.
takeaways: Prefer the most managed option that meets requirements: functions, Cloud Run, GKE Autopilot, then GKE Standard and Compute Engine.
Use custom machine types to avoid waste and Spot VMs for fault-tolerant batch workloads.
Committed use discounts reduce steady cost; sole-tenant nodes help with licensing and isolation.
Match special needs: GPUs and TPUs for ML, M-series for in-memory databases, VMware Engine for VMware estates.

lessons.title: Choosing Storage and Databases
lessons.summary: Cloud Storage, Filestore, Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, Spanner, Bigtable, Firestore, Memorystore.
takeaways: Object = Cloud Storage with classes and locations; file = Filestore and friends; block = Persistent Disk/Hyperdisk/Local SSD.

Cloud SQL for standard relational, AlloyDB for demanding PostgreSQL, Spanner for global scale and consistency, Bigtable for huge key-value, Firestore for documents, Memorystore for cache, BigQuery for analytics.
Cloud SQL scales writes vertically; Spanner scales horizontally with strong consistency.
Pair stores: transactional sources feed analytics through Datastream or Dataflow.

lessons.title: Choosing Data Processing and Analytics
lessons.summary: Pub/Sub, Dataflow, Dataproc, BigQuery, Composer and Dataplex.
takeaways: Pub/Sub ingests and decouples; Dataflow transforms; BigQuery analyses; Cloud Storage keeps raw data; Composer orchestrates.
Dataflow for new serverless batch/stream pipelines; Dataproc for existing Spark/Hadoop (ephemeral clusters on Cloud Storage).
Partition and cluster BigQuery tables and pick on-demand versus capacity pricing by workload pattern.
Govern with Dataplex, policy tags, row/column security and VPC Service Controls.

lessons.title: Cloud-Native Network Design
lessons.summary: VPC, subnets, Shared VPC, peering, Private Service Connect, firewalls and routing.
takeaways: VPCs are global, subnets regional; use custom mode, global dynamic routing as needed, and service-account-targeted firewall rules.
Shared VPC for central control, peering for simple non-transitive links, PSC for service publishing and overlap-safe access, NCC for hub-and-spoke.
Private Google Access, Cloud NAT and private services access remove the need for external IPs.
Plan GKE alias IP ranges and serverless VPC egress early.

lessons.title: Hybrid and Multicloud Connectivity
lessons.summary: Cloud VPN, Interconnect, Cloud Router, Network Connectivity Center and Cross-Cloud Interconnect.
takeaways: HA VPN is quick and cheap (99.99% with proper topology); Dedicated Interconnect for high steady bandwidth in a colo; Partner Interconnect via providers; Cross-Cloud Interconnect to other clouds.
Cloud Router with BGP provides dynamic routing; use global dynamic routing for multi-region VPCs.
99.99% Interconnect needs four connections across two metros; 99.9% needs two in one metro.
NCC connects spokes; Cloud DNS forwarding and inbound policies make hybrid name resolution work.

lessons.title: Migration Planning and Tooling
lessons.summary: Migration Center, the six Rs, migration tools, dependencies, licensing and cost.
takeaways: Assess, plan, migrate, optimise; use dependencies to define waves.
Pick rehost, replatform, refactor, repurchase, retire or retain per workload.
Know the tools: Migration Center, Migrate to VMs, VMware Engine, Database Migration Service, Storage Transfer Service, Transfer Appliance.
Compute transfer time, plan network, licences and TCO; always include testing and rollback.

lessons.title: Designing Generative AI and ML Solutions
lessons.summary: Gemini, Model Garden, Agent Builder, RAG and AI Hypercomputer in an architecture.
takeaways: Gemini (models), Model Garden (catalogue), Agent Builder (agents and search), prebuilt APIs and AI Hypercomputer (infrastructure) cover the AI portfolio.
RAG grounds answers in your data: ingest, chunk, embed, index, retrieve, screen, generate.
Prefer prebuilt APIs or prompting and RAG before fine-tuning or custom training.

title: Designing for Security and Compliance (Section 3, ~17.5%)

lessons.title: IAM and the Resource Hierarchy
lessons.summary: Roles, service accounts, conditions, deny policies and separation of duties.
takeaways: Allow policies inherit and union down the hierarchy; deny policies and organization policy restrict even allowed access.
Use predefined roles and groups; avoid basic roles; custom roles only when needed.
Dedicated service accounts, attached identities, impersonation and Workload Identity Federation replace service account keys.
Use conditions, PAM, Policy Troubleshooter/Analyzer and Recommender, and design explicit separation of duties.

lessons.title: Data Protection: Cloud KMS, Secrets and Sensitive Data
lessons.summary: CMEK, HSM, EKM, Secret Manager and Sensitive Data Protection.
takeaways: Data is encrypted at rest by default; escalate to CMEK, HSM, EKM or CSEK as control requirements grow.
Cloud KMS: keys, versions, rotation, scheduled destruction, location matching and separate admin/user roles.
Secret Manager for secrets; Sensitive Data Protection to discover and de-identify PII.
Confidential Computing protects data in use.

lessons.title: Perimeter and Access Controls
lessons.summary: VPC Service Controls, organization policy, hierarchical firewalls, IAP and Workload Identity Federation.
takeaways: VPC Service Controls add a network-context perimeter around Google APIs to stop exfiltration even with valid IAM credentials.
Organization Policy constrains configurations (locations, external IPs, key creation); hierarchical firewall policies centralise network rules.
IAP, context-aware access and Chrome Enterprise Premium implement zero-trust access without VPNs or public bastions.
Impersonation and federation remove long-lived keys.

lessons.title: Software Supply Chain and AI Security
lessons.summary: Artifact Registry, Binary Authorization, provenance and Model Armor.
takeaways: Secure each stage from source to runtime and verify at deploy: Artifact Registry, provenance, attestations, Binary Authorization.
Model Armor, Sensitive Data Protection and private, scoped model deployment secure AI systems; treat prompts and retrieved content as untrusted.
Security Command Center centralises posture, vulnerabilities and threat findings.
Use separate service accounts and key custody for attestations and models.

lessons.title: Compliance, Residency and Audit
lessons.summary: Regulation, Assured Workloads, audit logs and Access Transparency.
takeaways: Translate each regulation into concrete controls and use only in-scope services; compliance of the workload is yours.
Residency: gcp.resourceLocations, regional services, Assured Workloads, EKM.
Audit logs: Admin Activity always on; enable Data Access logs for sensitive services; centralise and lock retention.
Access Transparency and Access Approval add visibility and control over Google personnel access.

takeaways: Cloud Build → Artifact Registry → Cloud Deploy forms the managed pipeline; promote the same artifact through environments.

lessons.summary: A full design question across compute, data, network, security and operations.
takeaways: Trace every decision to a stated requirement and say which pillar or constraint it serves.
Cloud Run, Spanner, Pub/Sub and BigQuery give scale, consistency, decoupling and analytics with low ops.
Residency, PCI scope, hybrid coexistence and team skills are the hidden constraints that decide close calls.
Phase the migration with the strangler pattern to reduce risk.

lessons.title: Scenario: A Regulated Hybrid Healthcare Platform
lessons.summary: Compliance, hybrid connectivity, data residency and recovery.
takeaways: Combine residency, key custody, perimeter, de-identification, connectivity and audit into one coherent design.
Size availability and DR to the stated targets; avoid over-engineering.
AI features need de-identified inputs, screening and regional endpoints.
Exceptions use narrow ingress/egress rules and time limits, not wider perimeters.

lessons.title: Lab: Deploy a Secure Three-Tier Service
lessons.summary: Cloud lab: Cloud Run, private Cloud SQL, load balancer, Cloud Armor and Terraform.
takeaways: Restrict Cloud Run ingress to the load balancer so Cloud Armor cannot be bypassed.
Use private services access and Direct VPC egress for private Cloud SQL connectivity.
Dedicated service accounts and Secret Manager give least privilege and no embedded secrets.
Always verify by testing the blocked paths, then delete resources in dependency order.
